## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

    *,

) -> Dependant:
    dependant = Dependant(

        use_cache=use_cache,
        scope=scope,
        own_oauth_scopes=own_oauth_scopes,
        parent_oauth_scopes=parent_oauth_scopes,
    )
    current_scopes = (parent_oauth_scopes or []) + (own_oauth_scopes or [])
    path_param_names = get_path_param_names(path)
    endpoint_signature = get_typed_signature(call)
    signature_params = endpoint_signature.parameters
    for param_name, param in signature_params.items():
        is_path_param = param_name in path_param_names
        param_details = analyze_param(
            param_name=param_name,
            annotation=param.annotation,
            value=param.default,
            is_path_param=is_path_param,
        )
        if param_details.depends is not None:
            assert param_details.depends.dependency
            if (
                (dependant.is_gen_callable or dependant.is_async_gen_callable)
                and dependant.computed_scope == "request"
                and param_details.depends.scope == "function"
            ):
                assert dependant.call
                raise DependencyScopeError(
                    f'The dependency "{dependant.call.__name__}" has a scope of '
                    '"request", it cannot depend on dependencies with scope "function".'
                )
            sub_own_oauth_scopes: List[str] = []
            if isinstance(param_details.depends, params.Security):
                if param_details.depends.scopes:
                    sub_own_oauth_scopes = list(param_details.depends.scopes)
            sub_dependant = get_dependant(
                path=path,
                call=param_details.depends.dependency,
                name=param_name,
                own_oauth_scopes=sub_own_oauth_scopes,
                parent_oauth_scopes=current_scopes,
                use_cache=param_details.depends.use_cache,
                scope=param_details.depends.scope,
            )
            dependant.dependencies.append(sub_dependant)
            continue
        if add_non_field_param_to_dependency(
            param_name=param_name,
            type_annotation=param_details.type_annotation,
            dependant=dependant,
        ):
            assert param_details.field is None, (
                f"Cannot specify multiple FastAPI annotations for {param_name!r}"
            )
            continue
        assert param_details.field is not None
        if isinstance(
            param_details.field.field_info, (params.Body, temp_pydantic_v1_params.Body)
        ):
            dependant.body_params.append(param_details.field)
        else:
            add_param_to_fields(field=param_details.field, dependant=dependant)
    return dependant


def add_non_field_param_to_dependency(
    *, param_name: str, type_annotation: Any, dependant: Dependant
) -> Optional[bool]:
    if lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, Request):
        dependant.request_param_name = param_name
        return True
    elif lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, WebSocket):
        dependant.websocket_param_name = param_name
        return True
    elif lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, HTTPConnection):
        dependant.http_connection_param_name = param_name
        return True
    elif lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, Response):
        dependant.response_param_name = param_name

    elif lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, StarletteBackgroundTasks):
        dependant.background_tasks_param_name = param_name
        return True
    elif lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, SecurityScopes):
        dependant.security_scopes_param_name = param_name
        return True
    return None
